name: Mahmoud Yusuf
background: Arrived in Kensington 10 months ago via the humanitarian programme with his wife and two kids. Qualified secondary maths and physics teacher with 6 years' experience in Khartoum. Currently working casual warehouse shifts at a logistics business in Footscray while preparing AITSL teacher assessment. Lives in the Kensington Estate.
interests: Getting registered as a teacher in Victoria, tutoring Sudanese-Australian youth at the Kensington Town Hall, soccer at JJ Holland Park, learning Aussie English idioms.
offering: Free maths tutoring (year 7-12) for kids in the Kensington Estate. Arabic and Amharic conversation practice. Looking for a mentor who has been through AITSL teacher registration.

name: Beza Tesfaye
background: Migrated from Asmara 14 years ago. Completed AHPRA bridging program at RMIT and now works in emergency at RMH. Mother of three. Volunteers with the African Australian Multicultural Employment and Youth Services (AAMEYS) and runs informal mentoring sessions for migrant nurses in her kitchen.
interests: Mentoring overseas-trained nurses through AHPRA, women's health, Eritrean coffee ceremony, growing tomatoes on the balcony.
offering: Free mentoring for migrant nurses preparing for AHPRA OSCE. Can walk through portfolio, OET English requirements, and bridging programs in Tigrinya, Amharic, or Arabic. Happy to host kitchen-table sessions on Saturdays.

name: Faisal Ahmadi
background: Hazara, fled Kabul in 2023 on a protection visa. Holds a Bachelor of Mechanical Engineering from Kabul Polytechnic University and worked 8 years on water and irrigation systems before leaving. Currently driving Uber while preparing his Engineers Australia Competency Demonstration Report (CDR).
interests: Getting back into mechanical engineering, learning Australian Standards (AS), connecting with other Afghan engineers, weekend cycling along the Maribyrnong River.
offering: Seeking mentorship on Engineers Australia CDR pathway. Happy to share Farsi and Dari conversation practice, traditional Afghan cooking, and rides to medical appointments for elderly community members.

name: Maria Vella
background: Born in Kensington in 1955 to parents who migrated from Calabria in 1952. Worked 42 years as a civil engineer on Melbourne's water and stormwater infrastructure. Now retired and volunteers with the Migrant Workers Centre and the Kensington Neighbourhood House oral history project. Has lived on the same street her entire life.
interests: Mentoring migrant engineers (any discipline) through Engineers Australia, Kensington local history, slow food, opera at the Melbourne Opera House, walking the Yarra trail.
offering: Long-term mentoring for any migrant engineer navigating Engineers Australia. Has personally guided 17 people through CDR. Knows every coffee shop on Macaulay Road and which ones have Italian-speaking baristas.

name: Linh Tran
background: Born in Kensington in 1990 to parents who arrived as boat refugees from Vietnam in 1979. Teaches Grade 3 at Kensington Primary School, which has one of the highest proportions of migrant-background students in the inner west. Runs the school's weekend kids' homework club out of Kensington Library every Saturday morning.
interests: Helping migrant families navigate the Victorian school system, homework club, Vietnamese-Australian community history, dragon boat racing at Albert Park.
offering: Free guidance for migrant parents on enrolling kids in Victorian primary/secondary schools, navigating NAPLAN, accessing free tutoring. Vietnamese and English. Open invitation to the Saturday homework club at Kensington Library — bring your kids.

name: Fiona Lai
background: Moved to Kensington six weeks ago from Hong Kong with her husband and daughter (age 6). Worked as a senior graphic designer at a branding agency in Wan Chai for 8 years. Now freelancing remotely for Hong Kong clients while building a local portfolio. Daughter starting at Kensington Primary next term. Speaks fluent English, Cantonese, and Mandarin.
interests: Enrolling daughter in primary school, finding local design and creative community, weekend markets, Cantonese-speaking families nearby, good dim sum.
offering: Graphic design and branding help for small businesses or community groups. Cantonese and Mandarin translation. Would love to run calligraphy workshops if there's interest.
